title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0RC0RD_1LC0RB_0RE1RD_1LF1LE_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0RC0RD_1LC0RB_0RE1RD_1LF1LE_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and it is now proved in Lean to be a question about a simple map on lists of numbers. At the moments the head, in A, is at the left wall, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00. From one such moment to the next the list changes by a halving cascade: halve the first block, carry the other half into the next block, and go on halving while the value halved was even. Lean proves that the machine halts from blank tape iff the orbit of (1, 1) under this map reaches a cascade that runs past the last block with a carry that is a power of 2 (halts_iff). Iterating the map 6·1010 times from the start finds none.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 5,349 cells have been visited and 5,338 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.354). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.288).

claims.title: The halving round
claims.text: L 0 1^k 0 0 0 1^(m+2) D> 0 0 1^n R becomes L 0 1^(k+1) 0 0 0 1^m D> 0 0 1^(n+1) R in 2m+11 steps, for all k, m, n and any tapes L, R: two 1s leave the block being halved, one to each neighbour. Also the runs of D (right) and E (left) over 1s. Generated by py/rules.py.

claims.title: The run is the orbit of the cascade map (Lean theorem)
claims.text: Write Wall(ns) for 0^inf A> 0 0 1^n1 0 0 1^n2 … 0 0 1^nk 0^inf. For every list ns of blocks ≥ 1, if the cascade map F sends ns to ns′ the machine goes from Wall(ns) to Wall(ns′) (and ns′ has blocks ≥ 1), and if F ns = none the machine halts from Wall(ns). The blank tape is at Wall([1, 1]) after 13 steps. So the machine halts from blank tape iff the orbit of [1, 1] under F reaches none. The map in Lean is written the way the machine computes it (cascM, tailM, F); #eval of its orbit agrees with py/cascade.py. Proof: 13 rules generated by symtm (the halving round, the start at the wall, the even and odd ends, the gap move, the sweep back, the merge, the halt past the end), and a hand-written induction over the list.

claims.title: The cascade map, checked against the run (before the proof)
claims.text: At each moment the head, in A, extends the tape to the left, the tape is 0^inf A> 0 0 1^n1 0 0 1^n2 ... 0 0 1^nk 0^inf. The map of py/cascade.py predicts the next list exactly for all 1,779 such moments in the first 109 steps (from (1, 1) at step 13), and the machine's next list agrees with it for 1,500 random lists of 1 to 6 blocks (small and large values), halts included.

claims.title: When the machine halts
claims.text: In the Lean map, F ns = none exactly when an even halving runs past the end of the list with the value 2 (the next block would be 0): a block can become 0 only past the end of the list, where the carry c is halved again and again (new blocks c/2, c/4, ...) until it is odd; if c is a power of 2 it runs down to a block 0, which is a halt (past_end: the machine then reaches F reading 1 within 62 steps, for every tape to the left). Examples: [2], [2, 1], [4, 2], [6, 1] halt.

claims.title: No halt in 6·10<sup>10</sup> rounds
claims.text: Iterating the map from (1, 1) for 6·1010 steps (c/cascade.c, about 13 minutes) never makes a block 0; 778,155,275 cascades ran past the end of the list, and the smallest odd part of a carry there is 3. By the theorem above this is a run of the machine of that many wall visits without a halt (trusting the C program's arithmetic).

claims.title: The sum grows by 3 per step; halting is a question of chance
claims.text: A cascade keeps the sum of the blocks except for the final +2 and +1, so after t steps of the map the sum is 3t + 2, while the number of blocks stays small (5 to 9). About 1.5% of steps run past the end, with a carry of the order of the blocks; such a carry is a power of 2 with probability of order 1/carry. Summed over the future this expected number of halts grows only like the logarithm of the number of steps, so if the carries behave like random numbers the machine would halt eventually, but nothing here predicts when, and nothing rules out a hidden reason that keeps the carries away from powers of 2.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known, and now exactly a question about the map: does the orbit of [1, 1] under F ever run past the end of the list with a carry that is a power of 2? That reduction is a Lean theorem (halts_iff); the question about the map is open (Collatz-like).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape this machine keeps a short list of numbers on its tape and halves them in cascades, like the carries of a binary counter; it halts only if one carry is ever exactly a power of 2. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the cascade.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 5,349 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Proved in Lean: the run is the orbit of a map on lists of numbers; it halts iff a carry past the end is a power of 2.

sections.heading: A list of numbers
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head, in state A, steps onto a new cell at the left end. The tape then always reads

blocks of 1s separated by two 0s, and the list (n1, n2, ..., nk) is all that matters. The first time is step 13 with (1, 1); then (4, 1), (2, 1, 4, 1), (1, 1, 2, 6, 1), ... At step 109 it is a list of 5 blocks with the largest 2,063 long.

sections.heading: Halve, and carry while even
html: Between two such moments the head halves the first block: a gap of three 0s moves into the block, and each round sends one 1 to the left and one to the right (proved in Lean for every block length):

When the block is used up, half of it (rounded down) stays where it was and the other half has been added to the next block. If the value halved was odd the head turns back (the next block gets 2 more, the one after it 1 more). If it was even the head goes on and halves the next block, carried half included, and so on: a cascade, like the carry of a binary counter. For example

(4, 56, 1877, 6) → (2, 29, 953, 479, 482, 1): 4 is even, so 56 + 2 = 58 is halved; 58 is even, so 1877 + 29 = 1906 is halved; 1906 is even, so 6 + 953 = 959 is halved; 959 is odd, so it stops, adding 480 + 2 to a new block and 1 to the one after.

A first block 1 merges into the next: (1, x, y, ...) → (x + 3, y + 1, ...). This rule predicts every one of the 1,779 lists of the first 109 steps, and it is now a Lean theorem for every list (next section).

sections.heading: The only way to halt
html:
Inside the list every halved value is at least 2, so no block can vanish. Past the end of the list it can: a cascade that is still going when it passes the last block keeps halving its carry c into new blocks c/2, c/4, ... until it meets an odd number. If c is a power of 2 it runs down to 1, the next block would be empty, and the machine halts. So the machine halts exactly when, some day, a cascade runs past the end with a carry that is a power of 2.

This is proved in Lean, for every list: halts_iff says the machine halts from blank tape exactly when the orbit of (1, 1) under the map reaches such a cascade.

Each step of the map adds exactly 3 to the sum of the blocks (the sum is 3t + 2 after t steps), the list stays short, and about one step in 65 runs past the end with a large carry. A power of 2 is rare among large numbers, but not impossibly rare: if the carries were random, the expected number of halting chances would grow like the logarithm of the time. In 6·1010 steps of the map, far beyond anything a direct simulation can reach, no carry past the end was a power of 2. Whether one ever is, is a Collatz-like question.

sections.heading: How the reduction is proved
html: The proof follows one round of the machine piece by piece; every piece is a theorem for all values of its counts and every tape around it, generated by bbtools.symtm:

1. Start (wall_start): A> 0 0 1 1 R becomes 1 0 0 0 D> R: the gap 000 is cut into the first block.
  2. Rounds (halve): 0 1^k 0 0 0 1^(m+2) D> 0 0 1^n → 0 1^(k+1) 0 0 0 1^m D> 0 0 1^(n+1); by induction, r rounds move r ones each way (rounds).
  3. Even end (even_end): 0 0 0 D> 0 0 1 → 0 0 1 0 0 0 D>: the gap walks into the next block, whose halving starts.
  4. Odd end (odd_run, dgap): the next block grows by 4, the one after by 1, and E turns back.
  5. Sweep back (atom, atom1, wall_end): each gap moves one cell left, which leaves every block as long as it was; at the wall the head turns in A.
  6. Merge (merge_run) for a first block 1, and the halt (past_end): halving 2 past the end of the list runs into F reading 1.

The induction over the list (casc_correct, and tail_correct past its end) chains these pieces, and halts_iff turns “every round ends at the wall again, or halts” into “halts iff the orbit reaches none”. What remains open is purely about the map.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.354). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.288).
After 109 steps the tape spans 5,349 cells (3,817 left of the start, 442 right), with a density of 1s of 0.998.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A halving cascade on a list of numbers (blocks of 1s): halve the first, carry half into the next while the halved value is even; Lean proves the machine halts iff a carry that runs past the last block is a power of 2. No such carry in 6*10^10 map steps.
family: halving cascade (carry while even) on a list of blocks
